I'm not going to rephrase it that way, because I don't actually believe it. "It depends on the individual" sounds balanced, but it dodges the question of what actually works better for most people doing knowledge work.

Sure, some people like offices and some teams benefit from in-person collaboration. But on productivity, retention, and quality of life, remote wins pretty clearly. And yeah, a lot of return-to-office mandates really do seem to be about managers wanting visibility and control, not about output. Pretending both sides are equally meritorious wouldn't be more accurate — it would just be more polite.
